questions.question: In Indian economy, the sectors are divided into Private and Public on what basis?
questions.solution: In Indian economy, the sectors are divided into Private and Public on the basis of Ownership of enterprises. Total cost of ownership (TCO) is a financial estimate intended to help buyers and owners determine the direct and indirect costs of a product or system.

questions.question: Which method is used to measure agricultural income in India?
questions.solution: Factor incomes arise from production of goods arid services, and incomes are expended on goods and services produced. Three alternative methods of measuring national income are possible. Output method is used to measure agricultural income in India. This method is also called as production method and consists of three stages.

questions.question: GDP – indirect taxes + subsidies = ______
questions.solution: GDP at factor cost or basic prices are equal to market prices minus taxes on transaction of products plus subsidies on products. The sum of net value added in various economic activities is known as GDP at factor cost.

questions.question: Establishment of Chittaranjan Locomotive took place during which Five Year Plan?
questions.solution: The First Five-year Plan was launched in 1951 which mainly focused in development of the primary sector. Establishment of Chittaranjan Locomotive took place during this First Five Year Plan.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'Laissez Faire Policy'?
questions.solution: Laissez Faire Policy is the theory or system of government that upholds the autonomous character of the economic order and believes that government should interfere as little as possible in the direction of economic affairs.

questions.question: Which among the following is not appointed by the President of India?
questions.solution:
Option **1** is correct, i.e. __**Vice-President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Vice president is** not **appointed by the President.
 
• The **Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament**.
 
• Vice president is elected by means of the single transferable vote and the voting in such election is by secret ballot.
 
• **Article 63 to Article 71 **of the Indian constitution deals with the Vice-President of India.
 
• The Vice-President occupies the **second-highest office in the country.**
 
• He is accorded a rank next to the President in the official warrant of precedence.
 
• He is the ex-officio chairman of Rajya Sabha.

 
• "The Vice-President is elected for a term of five years" is the correct statement regarding the Vice-President of India.
 
• The Vice-President of India is India's second-highest constitutional office after the President.
 
• Article 63 of the Indian Constitution provides that 'there shall be a Vice-President of India.'
 
• The Vice-President shall act as President in the absence of the President on the grounds of death, resignation, defamation, or other circumstances.
 
• The Vice President of India is also the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• The current Vice-President of India is Jagdeep Dhankhar.
 
• The first vice president of India was Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.

questions.question: Which of the following article describes India also as Bharat?
questions.solution:
Option **1** is correct, i.e. __**Article 1**__.

__
 
• **Article 1(1)**__ describes that **India, that is Bharat**, shall be a Union of States.
 
• The Constitution of India declares India as a Union of States.
 
• The Indian federation is not the result of an agreement by the states, unlike the American Constitution.
 
• The states in India have no freedom to secede from the Union.
 
• Indian federation is an indestructible union of destructible states.

**Note:** The Demand for Dominion Status has been mentioned in the 1928 Motilal Nehru Report.

questions.question: Which of the following writ is issued by a higher court to a lower court?
questions.solution:
Option **3** is correct, i.e. __**Prohibition**__.

__
 
• The writ of **prohibition**__ is meant to direct a subordinate to stop doing something that the law prohibits. It is issued by a higher court to a lower court.
 
• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution has been described as the ‘heart and soul’ of the Indian Constitution by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.
 
• It gives a citizen the right to approach the Supreme Court to get resorted any of the fundamental rights in case of their violation.
 
• It is also known as; Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
 
 

 __Article__
 __Consists of__
 
 

 Article 32
 
 
Right to move the Supreme court for the enforcement of fundamental rights including the writs.

 
 
• habeas corpus
 
• mandamus
 
• prohibition
 
• certiorari
 
• quo warranto
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• Habeas Corpus: This writ is issued to produce a person who has been detained whether in prison or in private custody, before a court and to release him if such detention is found illegal.
 
• Mandamus: The writ of command is issued by supreme or high court when any government, court, corporation, or any public authority has to do a public duty but fails to do so.
 
• Prohibition: It is a writ issued with a view to restraining a person from holding a public office to which he is not entitled.
 
• Certiorari: The writ of certiorari can be issued by the supreme or high court for quashing the order already passed by an inferior court, tribunal or quasi-judicial authority.
 
• Quo-Warranto: The writ of quo-warranto can be issued by the supreme or high court for asking of by what authority or warrant. It is issued by the court to enquire into the legality of a claim of a person to a public office.

questions.question: 'The Loyal Muhammadans of India' was a newspaper by which of the following?
questions.solution: Syed Ahmad bin Muttaqi Khan, commonly known as Sir Syed, was an Indian Muslim pragmatist, Islamic reformist and philosopher of nineteenth century British India. He founded the Loyal Muhammadans of India newspaper.

questions.question: Who among of the following was the founder of society called 'Abhinav Bharat'?
questions.solution: Vinayak Damosar Savarkar was the founder of Abhinav Bharat who advocated the reconversion of the converted Hindus back to Hindu religion. Savarkar coined the term Hindutva.

questions.question: First battle of Panipat was fought between which two armies?
questions.solution: The first battle of Panipat was fought between the armies of Ibrahim Lodi and Babur. Ibrahim Lodi’s uncle invited Babur to teach Ibrahim Lodi a lesson and instead lead to the end of Lodi dynasty in India. Babur founded the Mughal Empire after defeating Ibrahim Lodi.

questions.question: Which of the following civilization is famous for its city/town planning?
questions.solution: Indus Valley Civilisation is the oldest know civilisation of India which is well known for its urban or city planning. The city was normally divided into two parts with runs running from North to South and East to West. There was a proper system of drainage and the houses were built in uniform structure.

questions.question: With which of the following is 'Van Mahotsav' associated?
questions.solution: Van Mahotsav is an annual tree - planting movement in India, which began in 1950. The name Van Mahotsava means Festival of forest. It was started by K.M. Munshi.

questions.question: Near coastal areas, temperature on land in day time gets reduced due to ________.
questions.solution: Land and sea breeze is a phenomenon that occurs on sea shores. Sea breeze is the breeze blowing towards the land from the sea, especially during the day owing to the relative warmth of the land. This cools the land surface during the day and thus provides a moderate type of climate to the coast.

questions.question: Which of the following city is located on the banks of river Potomac?
questions.solution: Washington DC, the U.S. capital, is located on the banks of Potomac River, bordering the states of Maryland and Virginia. Washington D.C. is famous for the neoclassical monuments and buildings.

questions.question: How much is the difference of time between any two consecutive longitudes?
questions.solution: Longitudes are imaginary lines drawn on the surface of earth in order to determine the time zone of a particular place. The difference of time between any two consecutive longitudes is 4 minutes.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a vestigial organ in human body?
questions.solution: According to Charles Darwin, Thymus Gland, Wisdom teeth, Pharynx and muscle of ear lobes were the vestigial organ in human body.

questions.question: Bile is produced by which of the following gland?
questions.solution: Bile is a fluid that is made and released by the liver and stored in the gall - bladder. It helps with digestion. It breaks down fats into fatty acids, which can be taken into the body by the digestive tract.

questions.question: Which of the following cells secret insulin?
questions.solution:
__Explanation:__

 
• The pancreas is a compound (both exocrine and endocrine) elongated organ situated between the limbs of the ‘C’ shaped duodenum.
 
• 99% part of the pancreas is exocrine while only 1% part is endocrine
 
• The exocrine portion (acini cells) secretes an alkaline pancreatic juice containing enzymes and the endocrine portion (islets of Langerhans) secretes hormones, insulin, and glucagon. islets of Langerhans have 2 types of cells α cells & β cells, the α cells surround the β cells
 
• Insulin is secreted by the β cells, while α cells secrete glucagon.
 
• Insulin is a hormone secreted by the Pancreas.
 
 
• It helps in maintaining the blood glucose level by stimulating the absorption of insulin by cells.

questions.question: Mass of an object is a ________.
questions.solution: Mass of an object is a Physical Quantity, Fundamental Quantity and Scalar Quantity. It doesn't change irrespective of place and time and doesn't have any direction specified to it.

questions.question: When a bus starts suddenly, then passengers in the bus tend to fall backwards. This event is an example of _______.
questions.solution: When a bus starts suddenly, then passengers in the bus tend to fall backwards. This event is an example of inertia of rest. Inertia of rest was proposed by Newton in his first law of motion.

questions.question:
Momentum of an object depends on which factors?

I. Mass of the object

II. Speed of the object

III. Velocity of the object
questions.solution: The momentum of an object depends on mass and velocity of the object It is a vector quantity. Its formula is p = mv.

questions.question: What is the approximate height of any geostationary satellite from earth’s surface (in km)?
questions.solution: A geostationary orbit, geostationary Earth orbit or geosynchronous equatorial orbit (GEO) is a circular orbit 35,786 kilometres above the Earth's equator and following the direction of the Earth's rotation.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to enter data and instructions into a computer?
questions.solution: Input devices are devices that feed information in a computer for completion of a task. Input devices like keyboard, mouse, light pen etc are used to enter data and instruction into a computer.

questions.question: Which among the following has largest storing space?
questions.solution: Tera mean 10^12. Tera byte is the largest storing space in any device followed by Gigabyte, Megabyte and kilobyte. Byte is the smallest storing place in a device.

questions.question: Which among the following is a pure element?
questions.solution: Sodium is a pure chemical element with the Chemical formula Na and atomic number 11. It is a soft, silvery - white, highly reactive metal.

questions.question: Sodium bicarbonate is chemical name of which of the following?
questions.solution: Sodium bicarbonate is chemical name for baking soda, bread soda, cooking soda or and bicarbonate of soda. Its chemical formula is NaHCO3.

questions.question: How is atomic mass number determined?

options.text: By adding number of protons and neutrons

questions.solution: The mass number is also called as atomic mass number or nucleon number. It is the sum of total of number of protons/electron and neutrons present in an element.

questions.question: Which of the following reaction is the main cause of energy radiated from Sun?
questions.solution:
• Nuclear fusion is a nuclear reaction in which hydrogen nuclei fuse together to form helium nuclei and release energy.
 
• In this state, some 120 million tons of matter - mostly hydrogen - is converted into helium on the sun every minute, with some of the mass being converted into energy.

questions.question: Plants which grow in salty water near sea shore are called as ______.
questions.solution:
A **halophyte** is a plant that grows in salty water coming into contact with saline water through its roots or by salt spray, such as in saline semi-deserts, mangrove swamps, marshes and sloughs and seashores.

 
 

 **Xerophytes**
 Any plant adapted to life in a dry or physiologically dry habitat (salt marsh, saline soil, or acid bog) by means of mechanisms to prevent water loss or to store available water.
 
 

 **Heliophytes**
 heliophytic plants, also called sun-loving plants, are those that require for their optimum growth full exposure to the sun. Examples are coconut, mango (Mangifera indica), sugarcane (Saccharum officinarum), corn (Zea mays).
 
 

 **Saprophytes**
 A saprophyte is an organism that survives by consuming nutrients from dead and decaying plant and animal material, that is, organic matter.

questions.question: How many biodiversity hotspot are present in India?
questions.solution:
A biodiversity hotspot is a biogeographic region with a significant reservoir of biodiversity that is under threat from humans. The four ecological hotspots are-

1) The Western Ghats and Sri Lanka

2) Indo Burma region

3) Eastern Himalayas

4) Sundalands

BIODIVERSITY HOTSPOTS IN INDIA : http://bsienvis.nic.in/files/Biodiversity%20Hotspots%20in%20India.pdf

questions.question: The Union Ministry of Human Resource Development has launched a nationwide 'Students for Soldiers: Vidya Veerta Abhiyan' to display portraits of ______ decorated soldiers in education institutes.
questions.solution: Prakash Javadekar, Union Minister of Human Resource Development, on 2 May 2017 launched the Vidya Veerta Abhiyan in New Delhi. Under ‘Students for Soldiers: Vidya Veerta Abhiyan' portraits of Paramveer Chakra recipient soldiers are decorated in education institutes.

questions.question: Who amongst the following gave the 'Periodic Law'?
questions.solution: Dmitri Mendeleev created the first periodic table. He arranged the elements by their mass and proposed that certain properties periodically reoccur. Mendeleev's table exhibits mostly accurate values for atomic mass and also has blank spaces for unknown elements.

questions.question: Which of the following pair is INCORRECT?
questions.solution: Bihu is the chief festival in the Assam state of India. It refers to a set of three different festivals: Rangali or Bohag Bihu observed in April, Kangali or Kati Bihu observed in October, and Bhogali or Magh Bihu observed in January. Bohag Bihu is the most important of all three as it celebrates the new year and coming of spring.

questions.question: In the 64th National Awards, which Hindi film has been awarded the Best Hindi Film for the year 2016?
questions.solution: The 64th National Film Awards was an award ceremony during which the Directorate of Film Festivals presents its annual National Film Awards to honour the best films of 2016 in the Indian cinema. Akshay Kumar was awarded as best actor and Neerja was awarded as the best film.

questions.question: The book 'Hope in a challenged Democracy' is authored by _____.
questions.solution: Hope in a Challenged Democracy is an Indian Narrative by an eminent lawyer, author and veteran parliamentarian, Dr. Ashwani Kumar. Hope in a Challenged Democracy is his second book that was released in April, 2017.

questions.question: With which country has India signed a bilateral contract for development and operations of Chabahar port?
questions.solution: Chabahar port is located in South-Eastern Iran, on the Gulf of Oman. In May 2016, India and Iran signed a bilateral agreement in which India would refurbish one of the berths at Shahid Beheshti port, and reconstruct a 600-meter long container handling facility at the port.

questions.question: 'Operation Pawan' was a peace-keeping operation by India in its which neighbouring country?
questions.solution: Operation PAWAN was the code name assigned to the operation by the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) to take control of Jaffna from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) in late 1987 to enforce the disarmament of the LTTE as a part of the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord. Operation Pawan' was a peace-keeping operation by India in its neighbouring country-Sri Lanka.
